scope: Bounded primary-source review for typed provenance/dependency graphs, reference-dependent derived summaries, and recovery of source records across local contexts
execution_policy: Read-only source inspection. No implementation, browser run, deployment, external communication, human study, Gate 7 work, or publication.

primary_sources.title: PROV-DM: The PROV Data Model
pins: Abstract and lines 34-38: provenance concerns entities, activities, and agents; the model includes derivations and bundles and permits domain-specific extensions.
Lines 596-626: entities have identifiers and attributes; activities act on or with entities and have optional time and attributes.

Lines 851-867: a derivation transforms, updates, or constructs one entity from a pre-existing entity; optional activity, generation, and usage make the derivation path explicit and aid provenance analysis and reproducibility.
Lines 1093-1119: a bundle is a named set of provenance descriptions and is itself an entity, so provenance of provenance can be expressed; its identifier identifies a unique set of descriptions.
supports: Representing each local source record, external requirement, reference definition, summary, correction, and run as typed entities/activities with stable IDs and attributes.
Making a reference-dependent summary a derived entity generated by a declared activity using the source records and reference/rule inputs.
Recording enough generation/usage/derivation detail that an inspector can follow the dependency path and reproduce or challenge the summary.
Keeping separate provenance bundles for alternative views or disagreements, with provenance attached to the bundles themselves.
does_not_support: A visual graph layout, expandable UI, or a claim that any particular typed link is socially meaningful.
Automatic truth of a summary merely because a derivation edge exists; provenance records describe production and responsibility, not validity of the underlying conclusion.
Calling the project’s cross-context graph a formal fiber bundle. PROV’s bundle is a named provenance set, not a topological fiber bundle.
primary_sources.use_in_gate6: Primary conceptual basis for typed local records, summary derivation, correction lineage, preserved disagreement, and provenance-of-provenance.

primary_sources.title: PROV-O: The PROV Ontology
pins: Lines 314-318: prov:Collection structures members; prov:Bundle is a named set of provenance descriptions that may itself have provenance, and adding/removing an assertion creates a distinct bundle.

Lines 320-324: prov:wasDerivedFrom has more specific forms including prov:wasQuotedFrom, prov:wasRevisionOf, and prov:hadPrimarySource; prov:specializationOf links a specific entity to a general one, while prov:alternateOf links aspects of the same thing.

Starting-point and expanded terms: prov:Entity, prov:Activity, prov:Agent, prov:used, prov:wasGeneratedBy, prov:wasAssociatedWith, prov:wasAttributedTo, prov:hadPrimarySource, prov:specializationOf, prov:alternateOf, and prov:hadMember.
supports: A typed vocabulary for distinguishing source records, reference-specific summaries, revisions/corrections, alternative serializations/views, collections, and the agents or plans responsible for them.

Versioned reference views: preserve the stable/general record entity and represent a context- or time-specific summary as a specialization or derived entity; preserve alternative summaries as alternate entities or separate bundles.
Recoverability requirements: retain member/source IDs and provenance assertions so a summary can be traced back to the same entities rather than treated as a self-contained label.
does_not_support: A domain-specific dependency taxonomy such as shared-source, depends-on, contributes-to, or correction; these need a declared application vocabulary and evidence rule.
A human-usability or comprehension result, a semantic attention model, or authority/influence inferred from graph position.
Formal fiber-bundle structure across local contexts; PROV:Bundle is a provenance container with a different meaning.
primary_sources.use_in_gate6: Primary typed relation vocabulary and version/alternate/specialization guidance for summaries and preserved disagreements.

primary_sources.title: Object Model
pins: Lines 44-52: the model represents Jobs and Datasets, and a lineage graph is created by weaving observations from many Jobs; RunEvent, JobEvent, and DatasetEvent separate runtime and design-time metadata.
Lines 55-64: each Run State Update is a distinct observation; subsequent updates are additive, and JobEvent carries source-code location, declared inputs/outputs, and documentation.
Lines 76-96: Jobs are named in a namespace; Runs are uniquely identified instances and preserve identity across state updates.
Lines 110-124: Datasets have namespace/name identity; static metadata is separated from run-specific input/output facets, including version information.
supports: An operational event shape for typed cross-context dependencies: local job/activity identity, stable run identity, input/output entities, source version, and additive observations.

Separating stable source facts and reference/rule metadata from run-specific changes, so corrections or changed external requirements can be added as new observations without overwriting the prior record.
A graph built from observed typed input/output relations, rather than from visual adjacency or an unlabeled edge.
does_not_support: The project’s fictional local-model semantics or its reference questions; OpenLineage is an operational data-lineage model.
A guarantee that forwarded metadata is authoritative or synchronized; the related Parent Run Facet states that the parent’s own event remains authoritative when forwarded facets differ.
A claim that source lineage proves a summary correct, useful, socially influential, or understandable.
primary_sources.use_in_gate6: Operational pattern for immutable IDs, additive event history, explicit inputs/outputs, version facets, and recoverable parent/child run relationships.

derived_gate6_requirements.design: Represent the summary as a new derived entity with summary ID/version, reference ID/version/wording/scope/criterion, rule version or hash, source record IDs/content hashes, producing activity/run, and attribution. The expandable view must traverse the explicit usage/derivation path and expose unknown/unmapped records.
derived_gate6_requirements.basis: PROV-DM derivation with explicit activity/generation/usage; PROV-O wasDerivedFrom and specialization/alternate; OpenLineage stable job/run/dataset identity.
derived_gate6_requirements.status: Application design derived from sources; not a behavior guaranteed by any source.

derived_gate6_requirements.claim: Similar summaries can hide different dependencies
derived_gate6_requirements.design: Include a held-out fixture in which two local summaries have identical or near-identical text but different typed input edges. The graph/table inspector must reveal the differing source IDs, rules, versions, and unresolved inputs; text equality alone must not collapse entities.
derived_gate6_requirements.basis: PROV-DM treats derivation as a relation with optional path detail; OpenLineage distinguishes inputs from outputs and event observations.
derived_gate6_requirements.status: Project test requirement; not an empirical claim about human recognition.

derived_gate6_requirements.claim: Changed external requirement and attributable correction stay linked
derived_gate6_requirements.design: Model the changed requirement as a new versioned entity. Link it to the local source record or activity that consumed it, the correction/revision activity, the corrected summary, and the responsible agent/plan. Preserve the prior summary/bundle and show what changed and why.
derived_gate6_requirements.basis: PROV-DM revision/derivation, usage/generation, attribution and bundles; OpenLineage additive observations and version facets.
derived_gate6_requirements.status: Application design derived from sources; no claim of causal or governance validity.

derived_gate6_requirements.claim: Unjustified cross-context links must be visible as unsupported
derived_gate6_requirements.design: A cross-context edge requires an explicit type, endpoints, evidence/source IDs, rule/version, and producing activity or declared assertion. If any are missing, retain the endpoint records but mark the edge unsupported/unjustified and make the absence inspectable in both graph and plain table.
derived_gate6_requirements.basis: PROV’s typed/entity/activity model and optional derivation-path detail; OpenLineage’s requirement to identify jobs/runs and inputs/outputs for lineage observations.
derived_gate6_requirements.status: Application integrity rule; not a standard conformance result.

gate2_context.fixture: Gate 2 retained four immutable fictional records extracted from the supplied repair-event facts: Hall, Field, Studio, and weather/task context.
references: R_CAPACITY_60: which venues hold at least 60 households
R_EXISTING_ACCESS: which venues already have wheelchair access without added equipment
gate2_context.observed_reference_behavior: The reference switch changed assignments/reasons while preserving record facts, source/history hashes, alternative mappings, and the intentionally unmapped weather context. Hall’s supplied ramp option remained visible when its existing-access result changed.
gate2_context.contextual_limit: Gate 2’s candidate semantic mapping is a declared interface rule, not a discovered attention model. Gate 6 should reuse this pattern for local contexts and typed dependencies without converting geometric or graph structure into claims about influence, agreement, authority, or human meaning.

limits: The standards support typed provenance and lineage descriptions, not the project’s UI, graph layout, summary wording, or human interpretation.

A provenance/dependency edge says what was declared or observed as used, generated, derived, revised, or related; it does not by itself prove correctness, causality, influence, agreement, authority, or commitment.

Reference-dependent summaries are an application design: the reference is an explicit input/rule/version and the summary is a derived artifact. The standards do not prescribe an expandable summary control or a recoverability threshold.

PROV:Bundle is a named set of provenance descriptions and is not a formal fiber bundle. Gate 6’s connected local-model graph should be described as bundle-inspired only unless a base, total space, projection, fibers, and required bundle structure are separately specified and verified.

OpenLineage is designed for operational data pipelines; mapping its Job/Run/Dataset vocabulary to fictional local contexts is an analogy/application choice, not a claim that the Looking Glass model is an OpenLineage deployment.
